raw_response:
I've been working this land for 30 years. I know my soil, I know my market, I know what my neighbors do. Quzhou gets dry in spring and I can't rely on rain, so my well is everything. Let me think through each crop.

**Cabbage** is my main income. Three rounds a year on my vegetable land — spring, summer, and autumn. I've done this long enough to know the rhythms. I buy hybrid seeds from the village supplier every year because the heads are bigger and more uniform, easier to sell. I put in more fertilizer than my husband thinks I should, but the soil here needs it and I've seen what happens when you skimp — you lose the whole harvest. I irrigate often; cabbage wilts fast in the Hebei summer. I spray when I see the white flies or the caterpillars starting, and I do a couple preventive sprays because once the pests spread, it's too late. I use rotary tillage before each planting — quick and good enough.

**Wheat** I keep on a small plot, mostly for household flour and a bit to sell. I use the improved variety the village sells — same one for years, I know how it behaves. I plough deep in autumn before sowing, then fertilize at sowing and top-dress in spring. Three or four irrigations: before winter, at jointing, at heading. I spray once for rust if I see it.

**Maize** follows on the same land after wheat, summer planting. Hybrid seeds. I fertilize well at planting and side-dress when it's knee-high. Fewer irrigations needed in summer because the rain helps. I spray for stem borer when the village broadcaster says to.
